rationale: Three lenses ran (blind/edge-case/acceptance). Blocking issue: AC4 explicitly requires regression coverage 'including native Claude Code launches,' but the entire new test matrix (claude-code-otlp.disable-matrix.test.ts) drives ClaudeCodeOtlpPlugin.processOtlpEvent() directly with synthetic hook JSON and mocked ensureOtlpProxy/forwardOtlpEventsToSpool — no test exercises a real/native Claude Code launch path. The acceptance lens independently marked AC4 'partial' on this basis. This is a decision_needed item (CR-001): is native-launch coverage achievable/in-scope for a unit-test task, or should it be explicitly deferred to manual QA/feature-verification with a note in the plan? AC1, AC2, AC3, and all out-of-scope constraints (personal-subscription, bulk ops, SSO session-sync channel, OtlpAgentAdapter.ts untouched) are satisfied with direct evidence. Six other findings surfaced (version-field forward-compat gap, hasClaudeCodeOtlpHooks/readClaudeAnalyticsPreferences conflating read-errors with absent/corrupt, no cross-process lock on the preferences read-mutate-write, non-canonical-entry equality risk, no path existence check, orphaned temp files on crash, status JSON conflating corrupt-with-disabled, redundant canonicalizePath calls) were triaged as defer/dismiss: each either mirrors an existing accepted codebase pattern (e.g. copilot-connector-scope.ts's own lock-free atomic write), is refuted by a real passing test (isProjectExcluded's nested-path case is directly tested against the real isPathInside, not mocked, in claude-code-otlp.preferences.test.ts), or is a minor error-message/UX quality issue with no functional-correctness or security impact given the gate already fails closed. One lens (blind) raised the isPathInside argument-order concern speculatively without repo access; the edge-case lens, which did have repo access and was asked to verify it, did not flag it, and the preferences test suite's real (unmocked) assertions on isProjectExcluded's nested/sibling/trailing-slash cases confirm the direction is correct — dismissed.

findings.summary: AC4 explicitly requires regression coverage 'including native Claude Code launches'; the implemented matrix only drives the plugin's processOtlpEvent() with synthetic payloads and fully mocked daemon/spool/SSO — no test exercises a real native Claude Code launch.
findings.recommendation: Decide with the user: either (a) add a minimal integration test that shells out to the actual hook CLI entrypoint (bin/codemie.js hook --agent claude-code-otlp) against a real settings.json + claude-analytics.json on disk, or (b) explicitly document this as a manual/out-of-automation-scope verification step (e.g. in the plan's Review Focus or a QA note) rather than leave it silently uncovered.
